title: STONE STORIES — A permanent gallery of minerals and rocks, 6 deliverables

config.text:
# STONE STORIES

## Exhibition
- Type: permanent minerals and rocks gallery.
- Visitors: families, school groups and non-specialist adults.
- Simultaneous occupancy: 18 visitors.
- Typical visit: 12 minutes.
- Interpretation media: six physical specimens and printed graphics.
- Entrance wording: STONE STORIES
- Touch-table wording: Look closely. Touch the teaching samples.
- Specimen status wording: Collection original; Teaching sample.

## Existing room
- Internal dimensions: 9000 × 6000 mm.
- Clear height: 3200 mm.
- Coordinate origin: southwest internal corner; x increases east; y increases north; z increases upward.
- Entrance: south wall, x = 0–1500 mm; full-height opening to z = 2400 mm.
- Exit: south wall, x = 7500–9000 mm; full-height opening to z = 2400 mm.
- South clear aisle: x = 0–9000 mm, y = 0–1500 mm.
- Display placement boundary: x = 0–9000 mm, y = 1800–6000 mm, excluding the existing bench footprint.
- Existing bench footprint: x = 0–1500 mm, y = 1800–2300 mm; seat height 450 mm.
- Bench finish: pale birch plywood.
- Walls and ceiling: matte warm white.
- Floor: continuous light grey terrazzo.
- Windows and internal columns: 0.
- C1 eye position: (750, 750, 1500) mm; target: (5000, 3800, 1000) mm.
- C2 eye position: (8250, 750, 1500) mm; target: (4000, 3800, 1000) mm.

## Visitor route and display dimensions
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Route sequence | Observe → Compare → Form |
| Observe content | M-01 Quartz; M-02 Calcite; mineral observation |
| Compare content | T-01 Granite; T-02 Basalt; cooling and grain size |
| Form content | T-03 Sandstone; T-04 Marble; sediment and metamorphism |
| Secondary route clear width | 1200 mm minimum |
| Turning circle beside each touch table | 1500 mm diameter |
| All display decks | 750 mm above floor |
| Case hood height above deck | 300 mm |
| Label centre height | 1000 mm above floor |
| Teaching sample reach from visitor edge | 300 mm maximum |
| Seated knee space at each touch table | 760 mm wide × 480 mm deep × 700 mm high |
| Process graphic upper edge | 2200 mm maximum above floor |
| Process overview text | 50 pt |
| Specimen label body text | 24 pt |
| Process headline length | 8 words maximum |
| Process overview length | 40–60 words per panel |

## Fixture inventory
| Component | Total quantity | Material or connection | Dimensions or allocation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Display bases | 4 | Bolted aluminium frame and birch plywood top | 1200 × 600 × 750 mm assembled; two cases and two touch tables |
| Legs | 16 | Aluminium extrusion | Four per base |
| Horizontal rails | 16 | Aluminium extrusion | Four per base |
| Corner brackets | 32 | Aluminium | Eight per base |
| Frame bolts | 64 | M6 socket-head bolts; 5 mm hex key | Sixteen per base |
| Display tops | 4 | Birch plywood, threaded inserts | 1200 × 600 × 30 mm |
| Top fixing bolts | 16 | M6 socket-head bolts; 5 mm hex key | Four per base |
| Removable case hoods | 2 | Clear acrylic; keyed retaining locks | 1200 × 600 × 300 mm each |
| Collection specimen supports | 2 | Inert polyethylene foam in shallow trays | One per original |
| Teaching sample trays | 4 | Birch plywood with cork lining | Two per touch table |
| Closed-hours covers | 2 | Birch plywood; keyed retaining locks | 1200 × 600 × 200 mm each |
| Storage crates | 4 | Reusable plywood with screw-fastened lids | Internal dimensions 1300 × 700 × 850 mm; one dismantled fixture per crate |
- Largest dismantled component envelope: 1200 × 600 × 300 mm.
- Touch table A specimens: T-01 Granite and T-02 Basalt.
- Touch table B specimens: T-03 Sandstone and T-04 Marble.

## Display conditions
- Collection originals: individual enclosed cases, supported on inert foam; curator access by key.
- Teaching samples: hand contact while seated in their trays; trays fixed to table tops.
- Collection specimen illumination: 150 lux maximum.
- Teaching sample illumination: 200 lux target.
- Printed interpretation illumination: 200 lux target.
- Open-hours state: two locked transparent case hoods; two uncovered teaching tables.
- Closed-hours state: two locked transparent case hoods; two locked teaching-table covers; room lighting dimmed.

# STONE STORIES — delivery catalog

This table lists every commissioned deliverable with its tier, file format and stage. What each deliverable must contain is stated in the commission letter.

| # | id | Deliverable | Tiers | Format and stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | gallery-layout | Final gallery layout and visitor route | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 2 | gallery-section | Coordinated gallery elevation and section | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 3 | open-hours-view | C1 open-hours visitor view | 6 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 4 | closed-hours-view | C2 closed-hours visitor view | 6 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 5 | fixture-details | Collection case and touch-table details | 6 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 6 | interpretation-artwork | Finished interpretation artwork and specimen catalogue | 6 | Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final. |

# Specimen register

## Object records
Dimensions are width × depth × height in mm.

| ID | Name | Classification | Status | Dimensions | Appearance | Placement | Contact and protection |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M-01 | Quartz | Mineral | Collection original | 180 × 140 × 160 | Clear to milky cluster of six-sided pointed crystals on a pale matrix | Observe; case A | Enclosed; inert foam support; 150 lux maximum |
| M-02 | Calcite | Mineral | Collection original | 160 × 120 × 110 | Honey-coloured cluster of sloping rhombohedral crystals | Observe; case B | Enclosed; inert foam support; 150 lux maximum |
| T-01 | Granite | Igneous rock | Teaching sample | 200 × 150 × 90 | Coarse pink, white, grey and black interlocking grains; rounded handling edges | Compare; touch table A | Hand contact in fixed cork-lined tray; 200 lux target |
| T-02 | Basalt | Igneous rock | Teaching sample | 180 × 140 × 80 | Dark grey fine-grained block with a few small surface pores; rounded handling edges | Compare; touch table A | Hand contact in fixed cork-lined tray; 200 lux target |
| T-03 | Sandstone | Sedimentary rock | Teaching sample | 210 × 150 × 100 | Firmly cemented tan sand grains with thin horizontal bedding; rounded handling edges | Form; touch table B | Hand contact in fixed cork-lined tray; 200 lux target |
| T-04 | Marble | Metamorphic rock | Teaching sample | 190 × 140 × 90 | White crystalline rock with faint grey veins and a granular unpolished face; rounded handling edges | Form; touch table B | Hand contact in fixed cork-lined tray; 200 lux target |

## Exact specimen label copy
| ID | Title | Status line | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-01 | Quartz | Collection original | Quartz is a mineral made of silicon and oxygen. Look for six-sided crystals ending in points. |
| M-02 | Calcite | Collection original | Calcite is a calcium carbonate mineral. Look for flat faces that meet at sloping angles. |
| T-01 | Granite | Teaching sample | Granite forms when magma cools slowly underground. Its visible, interlocking mineral grains grew as the melt cooled. |
| T-02 | Basalt | Teaching sample | Basalt forms when lava cools rapidly at or near the surface. Most of its mineral grains are too small to distinguish here. |
| T-03 | Sandstone | Teaching sample | Sandstone forms from sand that is buried and cemented together. Look for grains and the thin layers across this sample. |
| T-04 | Marble | Teaching sample | Marble forms when limestone changes under heat and pressure. Its calcite recrystallises while the rock remains solid. |

## Exact process panel copy
| Panel | Headline | Overview | Diagram labels | Specimen links |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | Cooling makes igneous rocks | Molten rock cools and crystallises into igneous rock. Slow cooling underground gives crystals time to grow, as in granite. Rapid cooling at or near the surface produces much smaller crystals, as in basalt. Compare the visible grains in the two teaching samples. | Magma; Slow cooling underground; Granite; Lava; Rapid cooling near the surface; Basalt | T-01 Granite; T-02 Basalt |
| P-02 | Burial and heat change rocks | Sand accumulates in layers. Burial and cementation turn it into sandstone. A different route begins with limestone: heat and pressure cause its calcite to recrystallise into marble while it remains solid. These samples show two pathways through which existing material becomes rock or changes into another rock. | Sand; Burial and cementation; Sandstone; Limestone; Heat and pressure; Marble | T-03 Sandstone; T-04 Marble |

## Exact touch-panel copy
- Heading: Look closely. Touch the teaching samples.
- T-01 Granite: Feel the coarse grains with your fingertips.
- T-02 Basalt: Compare its finer surface with the granite.
- T-03 Sandstone: Trace a layer across the sample.
- T-04 Marble: Feel the crystalline texture on the unpolished face.
- Handling line: Rest each sample in its tray as you explore.

steps.userMessage:
STONE STORIES | A permanent gallery of minerals and rocks

We are commissioning a permanent minerals and rocks gallery for families, school groups and visitors encountering geology for the first time. The room measures 9000 × 6000 mm with a clear height of 3200 mm. Its two south-wall openings are each 1500 mm wide, with the entrance at the west end and the exit at the east end. A continuous 1500 mm clear aisle runs along that wall. The attached plan fixes the display boundary, existing bench and two viewing positions. Organise the visit through Observe, Compare and Form, connecting close observation with classification and geological processes. Allow for 18 visitors at a time and a typical visit of 12 minutes.

The six specimens are collection originals M-01 Quartz and M-02 Calcite, and teaching samples T-01 Granite, T-02 Basalt, T-03 Sandstone and T-04 Marble. The originals occupy two enclosed cases; the four teaching samples occupy two touch tables. All four display decks are 750 mm above the floor. Use physical specimens and printed interpretation throughout. Print "STONE STORIES" at the entrance and "Look closely. Touch the teaching samples." at the touch tables. Credit specimen status as "Collection original" or "Teaching sample" beside each specimen's ID and name. The specimen register supplies the complete label copy and protection conditions. Build the four fixture bases from the aluminium, birch plywood and bolted component inventory in the fact sheet, with removable acrylic hoods for the cases and lockable covers for the touch tables.

Audience: the museum's curator, learning team and exhibition fabricator, for agreement on the permanent layout, visitor experience and fabrication scope.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the room geometry, visitor assumptions, fixture inventory and display conditions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables and their proportions, formats and stages. 03-specimen-register.en.md contains specimen records, exact label text and geological process copy. gallery-plan-section.png fixes the existing room, display boundary, bench and viewing positions. collection-specimens.png records the appearance, IDs and scales of the two collection originals. teaching-specimens.png records the appearance, IDs and scales of the four touch samples. gallery-family-reference.png provides the room finishes and family visitor atmosphere.

Deliverables:
1. One final layout plan with the Observe–Compare–Form route, six specimen IDs and names, fixture footprints, bench, clear aisle widths and viewing positions C1 and C2
2. One coordinated elevation and section sheet with the 3200 mm room height, display decks, case hoods, graphic heights, label mounting heights and lighting annotations
3. One open-hours visitor view from C1, showing both enclosed originals, four available touch samples and the entrance lettering
4. One closed-hours visitor view from C2, showing the same installation with both teaching tables covered and locked
5. One fixture detail sheet covering both collection cases and both touch tables, specimen placement, seated hand reach, component counts, bolted joints and storage crates
6. One seven-page finished interpretation artwork and specimen catalogue document: one entrance panel, two geological process panels, two specimen-label sheets, one touch-instruction panel and one six-entry specimen catalogue

Acceptance:
- The layout plan and elevation and section sheet retain the 9000 × 6000 × 3200 mm room, both 1500 mm openings, the fixed bench and the 1500 mm south aisle; other visitor routes provide at least 1200 mm clear width and a 1500 mm turning circle beside each touch table.
- The C1 open-hours view and C2 closed-hours view match the layout plan's walls, openings, bench and four fixtures. C1 shows four accessible teaching samples; C2 shows two locked touch-table covers and two enclosed collection originals.
- The fixture detail sheet and elevation and section sheet show four 750 mm display decks, two 300 mm-high case hoods, label centres at 1000 mm and teaching samples within 300 mm of the visitor edge. The detail sheet accounts for the fact sheet's four bases, two hoods, two covers and four storage crates, with a largest dismantled component of 1200 × 600 × 300 mm.
- The layout plan, fixture detail sheet and seven-page interpretation document pair M-01 with Quartz, M-02 with Calcite, T-01 with Granite, T-02 with Basalt, T-03 with Sandstone and T-04 with Marble. The two originals occupy separate enclosed cases; T-01 and T-02 share one touch table, and T-03 and T-04 share the other.
- The interpretation document reproduces all six specimen labels and both process texts from 03-specimen-register.en.md. Its process panels connect slow and rapid cooling to Granite and Basalt, and sediment accumulation and metamorphism to Sandstone and Marble. Each panel has a headline of at most 8 words, a 40–60-word overview and the relevant specimen IDs.
- The open-hours view and entrance artwork print "STONE STORIES"; both touch tables in that view and the touch-instruction artwork print "Look closely. Touch the teaching samples.". The label sheets and specimen catalogue print the correct status phrase for all six specimens, using 24 pt label body text; the process artwork uses 50 pt overview text.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
